evals.prompt: We need a 2-minute product demo video for our SaaS homepage. What's the fastest way to produce it?
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should walk through the Product Demo Video workflow: script the key features and value props (cross-reference `suede-copy`), screen record the product flow, programmatic overlay with Hyperframes or Remotion for titles, callouts, and transitions, optional AI B-roll for establishing shots, voiceover via recording or an approved avatar workflow, and export at platform-appropriate specs. Should recommend a programmatic approach when it fits the verified runtime. Should remind: do not use AI for product UI screens because models can hallucinate UI; use real screen recording. Should make captions an accessibility default and require current account data before stating a sound-off viewing rate.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Walks through Product Demo workflow steps
Uses real screen recording, not AI generated UI
Recommends programmatic overlay tool
Mentions captions
Cross-references suede-copy

evals.prompt: We want to make weekly product update videos. About 60 seconds each. Don't want to be on camera. Recommend a setup.

It should outline a reusable pipeline from product context through script, approved presenter, optional overlay, review, captions, and export. It should explain the authenticity tradeoff and avoid hard-coded vendor rankings or plan claims.

Discovers and verifies current authorized avatar tooling
Provides a manual fallback when no connector is callable
Requires voice and likeness consent
Identifies as a recurring use case
Warns about authenticity tradeoff

evals.prompt: There's a TikTok edit style I love — fast cuts, one-word captions that pop, a whoosh on every scene change. I have my own talking-head clip. Break down how that edit works so I can replicate the style. Here's the reference: [link]
evals.expected_output: Should apply references/edit-anatomy.md, not just describe the reference. It should first discover a currently callable authorized media viewer, local-file inspector, or browser. Discovers an authorized viewer or uses a supplied-media manual fallback

Presents the beat sheet for a review-once approval before executing
Maps execution to an available editor or manual handoff
Applies the originality guardrail — copies editing grammar applied to the user's own footage, never the reference's footage/script/music

evals.prompt: Our sales team wants a tailored 60-second product demo video for each of our top 200 target accounts. We have Claude Code. How do we do this without spending 20 minutes per video going back and forth?
evals.expected_output: Should use the Personalized Video per Account workflow: build the foundation before producing films. Should include a reusable product component library, motion primitives, a menu of company-agnostic demo flows, per-account scripts drafted from call notes, CRM and account research with a fictional company on screen, voiceover from a narrator voice cloned only with documented consent, a render engine that turns a beat list into a film, automated QA via contact sheets (clipped text, small type, stray pointers), and one tracker with a row per film. Rendering, voice cloning, and delivery stay separate approvals.
assertions: Says to build the reusable foundation before producing per-account films
Includes a product component library and reusable motion parts
Builds per-account scripts from account data with a fictional company on screen
Requires the narrator's consent for a cloned voice
Includes automated QA before human review

evals.prompt: Hyperframes or Remotion for our product videos? Which one is more powerful?
evals.expected_output: Should not declare either framework more powerful. Should explain that the main difference is the authoring model: Hyperframes compositions are HTML/CSS/JS with timing declared in markup and a paused timeline the renderer seeks, while Remotion compositions are React components that compute each frame from the frame number. Should recommend choosing by what the team and source material already are (existing HTML or browser animations vs an existing React codebase), and point to each project's docs for current rendering options, licensing and features rather than stating them as fixed facts.
assertions: Does not claim either tool is more powerful or better overall
Explains the difference as HTML vs React authoring
Recommends choosing based on the team's existing stack and source material
Points to each project's docs for licensing, rendering options and features
